God of the Scales of Pain, 
azaay azaay.

I begs you to take my pain for weighin’ so the killers who come done me harm get it back, right and fair. If I was you, I’d take yer star-tipped dagger and gut all ‘em raiders. All ‘em! ‘Til they guts is spilt and they eyes and tongues is pecked by buzzards! 

I gives you my pain to use and weigh. Pain from seein’ my husband’s head clubbed in by a raider as we was runnin’ to the ringfort that was clangin’ the raid bell. Pain from how the killer gone broke my arm and kneelt down ‘tween my pulled-apart legs. Pain from keepin’ his wild eyes on me, knowin’ my boy was hidin’, wartchin’ his Ma almost get took… ‘til a horn sounded and the savage scurried off like a rat... 

They was fast and quiet as a whisper… comin’ at night… stealin’ food… takin’ kids… 

All right and rulin’ Vikodin! Weigh my pain and hate! Give more strength to Hero B’zulo and his warriors. I prays they go on and fight and share our hurt with all them killers and raiders, so your Scales of Pain is even and fair.

I ain’t had no complaint ‘bout them Quentinites ‘til now. Harmless people got wronged by they’s maps. That’s what B’zulo says. They’s maps brought raiders here.

Obark ain’t for outsiders!

痛苦天秤之神，
阿賽，阿賽。

求祢拿我的痛苦去稱，讓那些傷害我的殺人犯，公平公正地受回去。若我是祢，就拿星尖匕首，剖開所有掠奪者的肚子。全部！讓腸子流出，眼和舌被鵟鳥啄爛！

我把痛苦交給祢，去用，去稱。警鐘響，我們往環堡跑，丈夫的頭被掠奪者砸爛的痛。兇手折斷我手臂，掰開雙腿，跪在中間的痛。我抓住他狂野的目光，知道兒子躲著，看媽媽差點被侵犯的痛……直到號角響，那野人像老鼠逃走……

他們快又靜，像耳語……夜裡來……偷食物……搶孩子……

公正統治的維科丁！稱我的痛與恨！賜布祖洛英雄和戰士更多力量。我祈求他們奮戰，把我們的傷痛分給殺人犯和掠奪者，讓祢的痛苦天秤平衡公平。

我從前對昆汀修士沒怨言，可現在，他們的地圖害了無辜人。布祖洛就是這麼說的。地圖把掠奪者帶來。

source:
The evening buzzards curiously sniff the day-baked vomit beside the well. 

the memory of it clings to me. 

A group of thin, dirty people called “slaves” approach the well. A haggard man wearing but a groin cloth lowers the bucket. His muscles quiver, veins bulge down his arms as he pulls the rope and draws the water. When he brings the bucket towards his chest, the bottom of it hits the stone wells’ lip and tips, spills. Water pours onto the feet of the guard beside the well. 

The guard of the well commands the man to get on his belly and drink the dusty slew. He hits the slave’s shoulder with the rod of his spear. “Them water’s worth more ‘n’ yer blood!”

Dust quickly makes mud of the spilled water. The man slurps it in. He curls up and wretches violently. The guard bends down, scoops a handful of mud and pushes it into the slave’s mouth, who immediately vomits mud and bile from his stomach. The guard jabs the butt of his spear into the slave’s ribs until he’s on his feet. 

These slaves return three times a day to fetch loads of water. They make clay bricks. Working to death to build a tomb. 

The human imagination for cruelty… 

I’ve seen a hawk tear the heads off of grackle birdlings with more kindness…

暮色裡，鵟鳥好奇嗅著井旁曬乾的嘔吐物。

那段記憶黏著我。

一群被叫作「奴隸」的瘦髒人走近井。憔悴男人只裹遮羞布，放下桶，拉繩汲水，肌肉顫抖，臂上青筋鼓起。桶拉到胸前，底部撞上石井緣，翻斜，水潑在守衛腳上。

守井人命令他趴下，喝沾塵的水，用矛桿打肩。「這水比你的血值錢！」

塵很快把水變泥。男人吸入口，蜷曲，劇烈乾嘔。守衛彎腰抓泥，塞進他嘴，奴隸立刻吐出泥與膽汁。守衛以矛尾戳肋，逼他站起來。

這些奴隸每天三次取水，製作泥磚。為建墳墓，工作到死。

人類對殘酷的想像力……

我見過鷹扯掉擬八哥幼鳥的頭，都比這仁慈……

source: Nav’ed Praetis: My dear friends and followers of the Quentinite Virtues. I called you all here firstly and foremostly to give my deepest gratitude for making this underground ancient structure, this “bunker” as it were, a home for me and the treasures of books, maps, and scripts we hold so dear. I like to imagine that the spirit of Quentin Brown smiles proudly at our work. For years, I was deeply forlorn after losing my eyes. Why, the very sense needed to read, to keep myself learning, was viciously cut from my body. I felt alone in a darkness that penetrated my heart, and I found myself thinking fondly of death. At least in death, I reasoned, I was not so conscious of my suffering. But my little Savyna and you all kept me listening. You all kept me learning through conversations of your insights and stories of wisdom. You all brought me back to life. Without my eyes, I saw more with my mind. Now I have something to give back. As I was listening to my daughter learn new words and gain new ideas, I began to ponder about learning itself. Inevitably, my musings led me to consider the limitations of how we convey learning. I thought deeply about language. Consider this: our minds are like dry roots, eager to absorb and grow from the waters of knowledge. Language is like the dirt that holds us and collects the water for us to take in at our own pace. Language and the absorption of knowledge, like soil and growth, are inextricably linked. Now, what if we could manipulate our language, this dirt -- till it, irrigate it, refine it so that knowledge flows unobstructed and intentionally between minds, the way water floods all roots in a well-trenched field? All crops, all minds, grow strongly and together with great efficiency. I have structured in my thoughts a framework for a new way to learn. A language that intends to capture the resonance of poetry, the precision of mathematics, and the utility of science. A way to exchange meaning rapidly and precisely, without obstructions from subjectivity. Brother and Sister Quentinites, let me tell you about the language I call Exomnus…
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：親愛的朋友，昆汀美德的追隨者。召集各位，首要是獻上最深謝意。你們把這座地下古建築，所謂「地堡」，變成我與珍貴書本、地圖、文稿的家。我喜歡想像，昆汀・布朗的靈魂，正驕傲地微笑看著我們。 失去雙眼後，我多年來深陷絕望。能閱讀、能持續學習的感官，竟被殘忍地從身上挖去。黑暗穿透心底，我孤獨，甚至開始嚮往死亡。我想，至少死後，不必如此清醒地感受痛苦。但小莎維娜和各位，讓我繼續聆聽。你們的見解與智慧故事，讓我繼續學習。你們讓我重新活過來。 沒有眼睛，我的心卻看見更多。如今，我也有東西能回報。 聽著女兒學新字、獲得新想法，我開始思考學習本身。思索自然引我考慮，我們傳授知識的方式有何局限。我深入思考語言。 想想：心智如乾根，渴望吸收知識之水而成長。語言如土，支撐我們，收集水，讓我們按自己的步調吸收。語言與知識吸收，如土壤與生長，密不可分。若能改造語言，改造這土壤——翻耕、灌溉、精煉，讓知識有目的、無阻礙地在心智間流動，如溝渠完善的田野，水流遍每條根呢？所有作物、所有心智，都能強健、共同而高效地成長。 我在思想中建立了新學習方式的架構。一種結合詩的共鳴、數學的精確、科學的實用的語言。迅速精準交換意義，不受主觀阻礙。 昆汀兄弟姊妹，讓我介紹這種語言，我稱它為艾克索姆語……
